title: Soroban 1:4 Orientation & Reckoning Beam
subtitle: Explore the rods and learn which beads count toward a number.
challenge: How does a Soroban represent numbers using a single upper bead and four lower beads?
predictionPrompt: When are beads counted toward the active value on a Soroban?

predictionOptions.label: When pushed toward the outer frame
When moved toward the reckoning beam

formalDefinition: A Soroban rod has 1 upper bead (value 5) and 4 lower beads (value 1 each). Beads are active strictly when moved toward the central reckoning beam.

steps: Neutral state: all upper beads pushed UP; all lower beads pulled DOWN (reads 0).
To set 7: move upper bead DOWN (5) and two lower beads UP (2).
workedExample.result: Rods represent powers of ten from right to left.

misconception.mistake: Counting beads pushed against the outer wooden frame.
misconception.correction: Only beads touching or shifted toward the central reckoning beam are active.

reflection: The 1:4 Soroban bi-quinary system minimizes finger travel and provides instant tactile feedback.
prerequisiteCheck: Read base-ten place values. A rod value is multiplied by its position; the units marker matters.
representation: For 15, the tens rod has one lower bead at the bar, and the units rod has the upper bead at the bar. Contributions: 1 × 10 + 5 × 1.

faded.prompt: Tens rod: upper away, 2 lower engaged. Units: upper engaged, 3 lower engaged. What number is represented?
faded.solution: Tens digit 2 gives 20; units digit 5 + 3 = 8; total 28.

independent.solution: Tens: upper engaged and 1 lower engaged (digit 6). Units: upper away and 4 lower engaged (digit 4).

independent.prompt: Does the upper bead contribute 5 or 50 on the tens rod?
independent.solution: 50. Its digit contribution 5 is multiplied by the tens place weight 10.

explanation: Explain why a bead away from the bar contributes zero, even though it remains physically on the instrument.

transfer.prompt: Move the units marker so the rightmost rod is tenths. Read left rod digit 1 and right rod digit 5 on a two-rod instrument.
transfer.solution: The left rod is now units and the right rod tenths: 1 + 5/10 = 1.5, not 15.

retrieval: Tomorrow describe how to set 37. A week later compare a rod digit with its place-weighted contribution.
reviewNote: Expanded prototype lesson. Independent mathematical, pedagogical, and accessibility review is pending.
